Review question: Does the broad immune and platelet RNA represent endogenous ACRBP expression?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve normal-cell RNA identity and reliable local protein evidence before changing the general exclusion.
Limitations: The retracted PMID 35463688 is excluded; the decision uses pinned RNA. Platelet RNA does not establish peptide presentation.

Review question: Why is RNA repeatedly detected in monocytes and naive B cells despite reproductive-positive curated IHC?
Reconsideration evidence: Review gene-specific read mapping and obtain reliable protein evidence in the implicated immune populations.
Limitations: DICE observations are not paired RNA/IHC donors; negative bulk-organ IHC does not assess every sorted immune population.

Review question: Are the few activated-CD4 values and Monaco plasmacytoid-DC summary reproducible?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve the borderline immune RNA with source-specific read review and reliable local protein evidence.
Limitations: Three of 88 activated-CD4 DICE values reach 5 TPM; this is a review threshold rather than demonstrated toxicity.

Review question: Does the Monaco-only borderline signal reflect genuine immune expression?
Reconsideration evidence: Reconcile Monaco CD8/basophil RNA with the much lower DICE values and obtain relevant protein evidence.
Limitations: Monaco summary values 5 and 6 TPM are weaker evidence than recurrent high original-sample RNA; DICE does not sample basophils.

Review question: What explains high basophil RNA in HPA and Monaco?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve basophil RNA identity and local protein evidence before reconsideration.
Limitations: TPM and nTPM are separate measurements; DICE has no basophil population.

Review question: Is the naive-B-cell RNA translated in normal B cells?
Reconsideration evidence: Review gene-specific mapping and reliable protein evidence in naive B cells.
Limitations: Reproductive-positive Enhanced IHC does not establish absence in the particular sorted immune cells measured by RNA.

Review question: Which primary antibody staining is specific to FOXR2?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve discordance between HPA034487 and HPA057358 using independently validated protein evidence.
Limitations: Both profiles are Uncertain; reproductive/tumor publication support does not validate normal-organ staining or waive counterevidence.

Review question: When and why do some normal heart specimens contain CTAG2 RNA?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve donor variability and obtain paired RNA/protein information from the implicated cardiac context.
Limitations: RNA donors and negative-IHC donors differ; neither absence of established target-mediated toxicity nor separate negative specimens clears the positive RNA donors.

Review question: Is the immune signal correctly assigned within the GAGE family?
Reconsideration evidence: Review uniquely assigning reads and exact gene/protein identity before reconsidering local expression.
Limitations: Highly related paralogs can complicate attribution; no paralog substitution or RNA-to-protein inference is permitted.

Review question: Are borderline DICE B-cell RNA and other cell-context signals genuine?
Reconsideration evidence: Review exact loci and source-specific normal-cell signals; reliable protein evidence must address implicated cells.
Limitations: A borderline immune summary must not hide a higher signal elsewhere; complete RNA audit accompanies this record.

Review question: Does its broader normal-cell expression permit a reproductive-restricted classification?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve the documented non-permitted cell expression before any reproductive-restricted designation.
Limitations: Tumor relevance and reproductive enrichment do not establish normal-cell restriction.

Review question: Can the uncertain primary-antibody normal staining be resolved?
Reconsideration evidence: Use independently validated protein evidence to adjudicate primary staining conflicts.
Limitations: An uncertain antibody is not reliable proof of either expression or absence.

Review question: Does the full normal-cell distribution support reproductive restriction?
Reconsideration evidence: Review diffuse RNA and missing reliable protein evidence rather than selecting the largest reproductive value.
Limitations: A high reproductive maximum does not erase normal-cell expression; no clinical safety conclusion is recorded.

Review question: Is the colonic undifferentiated-cell RNA correctly attributed and endogenous?
Reconsideration evidence: Resolve the pinned high normal-cell signal and exact locus/protein identity before reconsideration.
Limitations: Clinical interest does not create a gene exception; RNA does not by itself establish protein or peptide display.

Review question: Is the salivary serous-cell RNA above 30 nTPM a genuine local signal?
Reconsideration evidence: Review the underlying cluster and gene-specific reads with reliable local protein evidence before reconsideration.
Limitations: The value is close to the hard ceiling; a general rule is applied rather than a benchmark exception.
